rationale: Chronic CSF stability (5-year target) of immobilized enzyme is the SINGLE BIGGEST UNKNOWN in P-04. No published data on any enzyme immobilized in CSF-like conditions for >30 days.

csf_environment_factors.challenge: Accelerates protein denaturation. Most enzymes lose >50% activity in 30 days at 37°C in aqueous solution.
Slight deviation from many enzymes' pH optimum. Long-term pH drift possible.
May affect enzyme conformation and immobilization matrix integrity.
Immobilized enzyme may be degraded by endogenous CSF proteases over time.
Biofilm may cover enzyme surface, blocking substrate access.
May mechanically degrade immobilization matrix over time.

what_replacement_strategy_looks_like: If 5-year stability is unachievable, the design must include a REPLACEABLE enzyme cartridge — a small reservoir accessible via subcutaneous port, refreshed every 6-12 months. This is a SIGNIFICANT design change with major regulatory implications (combination product, replacement procedure, training).
blocking_work_required: Build synthetic CSF test loop (37°C, pH 7.33, pulsatile flow, sterile)
Test candidate immobilized enzyme for 30, 90, 180 days
Measure: activity retention, leaching rate, biofilm formation, mechanical integrity
Decision point at 90 days: is 5-year stability plausible, or is replacement cartridge required?
estimated_time_to_unblock: 6-12 months (longest single item in the freeze list)
constitutional_basis: Article XXXIV — this is the dominant reality bottleneck. P-04 cannot proceed to prototype until this is resolved.
